anchor.description: A repo-relative file:line citation, or null when the fact could not be anchored to source. null MUST be paired with an entry in the row's gaps array explaining why.

path.description: Path relative to the root of the repo that OWNS this inventory file (ops rows -> ops repo, web rows -> web repo, acr rows -> acr repo). A citation into a different repo is written repo-qualified in a note or in issued_credential.verified_by, never here.

accepted_credential_classes.description: class_id values from contracts/auth/v1/credential-classes.json this route's intended validator accepts. Empty for a genuinely public route.

action.description: Bounded action/permission this route performs, where the code names one explicitly (e.g. an Action/Scope enum). null + gaps note otherwise.

current_state_cache_behavior.description: TRD §14 cache class, where applicable (e.g. epoch_scoped, no-cache webhook, stateless). null + gaps note otherwise.

disclosure_behavior.description: Safe 401/403/404 disclosure behavior (TRD §18), where determinable at the family level.

entitlement_requirement.description: A licensing/gating.py feature key gating this route, where present. null when none.

exposure.description: Whether this surface is reachable from the PUBLIC INTERNET. This is decided by the EDGE PATH-MAP, not by whether the app mounts the route: two routes in the same app can differ. Proven case -- /api/v1/telemetry/* answers a live unauthenticated request through the edge (200 + body, 2026-09-01), while /api/v1/ingest/* on the SAME app is private-network-only and never publicly routed. A coverage claim that does not separate these conflates two different threat classes: an unauthenticated route behind a private network is a defense-in-depth item, the same route at the edge is an incident. The `source` field is REQUIRED and must name the artifact the claim was read FROM -- an asserted security boundary with no cited source is the defect class this whole inventory exists to prevent.

reachability.description: unknown is a legitimate value and MUST be paired with a gaps entry; it is the correct answer whenever the edge path-map was not consulted. Never infer public reachability from a route being mounted, and never infer private from it being internal-sounding.

source.description: The artifact this was read from -- edge/ingress path-map config, or a dated executed probe with its result. NOT a repo file that merely mounts the route: none of the ops/web/acr repos contains the edge path-map, so a repo-only citation cannot support a reachability claim.

gaps.description: Every field on this row that could not be anchored/determined in this pass, with a reason. Empty array means fully determined for this row.

id.description: Stable id: '<METHOD> <full_path> [<service>]' for REST (service-qualified because the same method+path can be registered on more than one deployed app -- see /api/v1/billing/webhooks/stripe and each app's own '/health'), 'graphql:<field|mutation>:<name>' for GraphQL, 'server_action:<repo-relative module path>#<exported function name>' for Next.js Server Actions (module path + export name, NEVER the per-build action id, which changes on every build). Never renamed once a CI gate references it.

impersonation_policy.description: Whether ImpersonationMiddleware's org-context override (api/middleware/impersonation.py) can affect this route. Every main-app route is technically subject to the middleware running (it has no path exemption), but only routes that read the org_id contextvar are actually affected by an override.

issued_credential.description: Every credential this surface MINTS, inbound-facing profile's mirror image. THREE distinct values, do not conflate them: a non-empty array lists the mints; [] means the surface was ASSESSED and positively issues nothing; null means issuance was NOT determined in this pass and MUST be paired with an entry in the row's gaps array, exactly like a null anchor. The property is OPTIONAL in v1 (added after the ops/web/acr inventories were frozen, so an untouched row is absent rather than wrong) -- absence means the repo's pass predates the field. Backfilled only where issuance was PROVEN by tracing the mint site, never by family pattern.

method.description: HTTP verb for REST (upper-case), or 'api_route' when the route registers a runtime method list. null for GraphQL and for server_action.

primary_validator.description: The route's OWN intended validator (may be a router-level dependency shared by every route in its family, in which case the anchor points at the dependency function, not this specific route). null for a genuinely public route with no validator at all.

reachable_validators.description: EVERY validator that can observe/attempt to process this route's credential before or instead of its intended one -- the CHAOS-3271 class. Derived from the middleware stack (CorrelationId -> OrgId -> Impersonation -> SlowAPI -> OriginValidation/CSRF -> GraphQLQuerySizeLimit -> SecurityHeaders -> CORS -> route, per api/_middleware.py) and mount path, not from re-reading the route body. Empty only for billing-edge-app routes, which share no middleware with the main app.

resource_resolver.description: How the target resource/org is resolved from the request (path param, body field, credential claim). null + gaps note otherwise.

route.description: Full resolved mount path for REST (e.g. '/api/v1/admin/teams'). null for GraphQL, which has no HTTP path, and null for server_action, which is dispatched by action id rather than path.

service.description: Which DEPLOYED APPLICATION serves this surface. Profiles are per-app, not per-path: the same logical route can appear under two apps with different middleware stacks (see /api/v1/billing/webhooks/stripe, served by both dev-health-ops-api with the full middleware stack incl. OrgIdMiddleware/ImpersonationMiddleware, and the separately-deployed dev-health-ops-billing-edge with ZERO shared middleware). This is a CLOSED vocabulary -- an unknown service must fail validation rather than be accepted, per guardrail G-26. Adding a newly deployed app means adding it here first.

surface_kind.description: server_action covers Next.js Server Actions ('use server'). They ARE auth surfaces and count toward coverage, but they are NOT method+path surfaces: Next.js dispatches them by an opaque per-build action id that changes every build, so a gate can never key on it. Key them on what IS stable in source -- module path + exported function name -- and leave method/route null.

token_shape.description: Issuer/audience/token-type/algorithm, where determinable and applicable (TRD §10). null fields inside the object are fine; the object itself is null when no field applies at all (e.g. a public route, or an HMAC-signature route with no issuer/audience concept).

issuedCredential.description: ONE credential this surface MINTS. The rest of this schema models what a route ACCEPTS; an auth control plane must also know what each surface ISSUES (guardrail G-12: signing keys are issuer-only; G-61: one active issuer per token class). Anchor the MINT SITE -- the line that signs/creates the credential -- not the line that sends it.

class_id.description: class_id from contracts/auth/v1/credential-classes.json, the same closed vocabulary accepted_credential_classes draws on. A minted credential with no class there is a Wave 0 finding, not a value to invent.

direction.description: outbound_to_dependency: minted to authenticate THIS service's own call to a downstream dependency (the caller never sees it). returned_to_caller: handed back to the requester in the response body, a header, or a Set-Cookie.

key_source.description: Where the signing key/secret comes from -- an env var NAME, a JWKS path, or a key-management surface. NEVER a key value.

lifetime_seconds.description: Nominal validity window at mint time, where the code sets one literally. null + a gaps entry when it is configuration-driven or not determinable.

verified_by.description: Repo-qualified file:line of the counterpart that VALIDATES this credential, when it is known and lives in the Wave 0 read set (e.g. 'acr:internal/auth/web_assertion.go:96'). null + a gaps entry when the verifier was not located.

reachable_but_not_owner.description: true marks a CHAOS-3271-class finding: this validator can observe/attempt to parse the credential before (or regardless of) the route's own intended validator, without owning that credential's class.

description: CHAOS-3273 Wave 0 freeze of every REST route and GraphQL resolver discovered under dev-health-ops's src/dev_health_ops/api, as of the anchors' commit. Guardrail G-1: a route without a registered profile fails CI and may not ship. Rows are generated from ci/discover_ops_routes.py's independent source discovery (contracts/auth/v1/endpoint-profiles.ops.json is NOT hand-maintained; regenerate + re-annotate rather than hand-editing paths/methods/anchors). accepted_credential_class values are a closed vocabulary keyed to contracts/auth/v1/credential-classes.json's class_id field -- a class not there is a Wave 0 finding, not a value to invent. Produced by lane auth-cp/L1; do not hand-edit without re-verifying anchors.

credential_class_source.description: Path to the closed-vocabulary credential-class file rows' accepted_credential_classes are drawn from.

source_commit.description: The exact ops commit rows were discovered/annotated against.
